bullets.title: MU: Blowout Q3 earnings, $100B in strategic customer agreements, AI supply tight through 2028
bullets.body: Micron reported F3Q revenue of $41.46B (+15% vs $35.9B consensus) and EPS of $25.11 vs $20.86, with 84.9% gross margin (+320bps vs consensus). F4Q guidance of $50B revenue and $31 EPS both ~15-20% above street. Management disclosed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs/LTAs) covering ~20% of DRAM and ~33% of NAND volume over 5-year terms, representing ~$100B minimum committed revenue at floor-price GMs 'well above any prior cycle peak.' Supply-demand tightness expected to persist beyond CY27 with 'no line of sight' on catch-up; HBM TAM pulled forward to $100B+ in 2027. MU committed to returning 100% of excess cash post-Dec 9 Chips Act anniversary. Price targets raised broadly: Citi $1,400 (from $1,200), KeyBanc $1,600, Wolfe $1,500, UBS $1,625 (street high), JPM $1,540, Mizuho $1,375.

bullets.title: AAPL: Raises Mac/iPad prices 15-25% on memory cost shock; iPhone 18 repricing looming
bullets.body: Apple announced price increases of 15-25% on MacBooks, iPads, HomePod, and other hardware, citing data center-driven memory/NAND cost inflation. iPhone prices were not raised initially, but management left door open for September iPhone 18 launch increases of $100+. Analysts note this is earlier and larger than expected; JPM, MS, and Citi all flagged that prior mid-single-digit iPhone price increase assumptions were too low. Bears see demand destruction risk (elasticity >1) while bulls cite carrier installment financing as a buffer. Stock fell ~6% on the announcement and further into week end. KGI downgraded to Neutral.

bullets.title: SNDK: Citi raises PT to $2,500; NAND supply tight through CY27 on AI-driven datacenter demand
bullets.body: Following Micron's results, Citi raised SNDK PT to $2,500 (from prior) and opened a 90-day upside short-term view, citing NAND supply/demand tightness expected beyond CY27. CY26 industry NAND bit shipments expected to grow 20%; MU's own NAND supply growth expected below industry average. SanDisk's New Business Model agreements feature fixed prices, cap-and-floor structures, and decommit penalties. JPM raised SNX (TD Synnex) PT to $325 on F2Q beat of $19.6B (+31% y/y) and accelerating Hyve hyperscaler ramps.

bullets.title: Mag 7 / Tech selloff: NVDA -8.6%, GOOGL -8.3%; megacap AI basket underperforms SPX by 9% MTD
bullets.body: The week saw the largest Info Tech and Comm Services net selling in over 10 years per GS Prime. NDX realized ~18 vol points higher than SPX, widest spread in two decades. Mag 7 collectively shed >$1T in market cap and were net sold for the fifth straight week with gross/net exposures approaching three-year lows. AI datacenter equipment stocks (GSTMTDAT) underperformed S&P ex-AI by ~11pp since June 22 highs. The selloff was driven by: (1) AAPL/MSFT hardware price hikes raising margin concerns, (2) OpenAI IPO delay to 2027, (3) leveraged ETF short gamma at record highs (~$16B/1% move), (4) GOOGL AI talent departures to Anthropic/OpenAI, and (5) Korean KOSPI -10% on leveraged ETF unwind.

bullets.title: AVGO: Unveils 'Jalapeño' AI inference chip with OpenAI; XPU diversification thesis validated
bullets.body: Broadcom and OpenAI unveiled Jalapeño, OpenAI's first custom LLM inference processor, with early testing showing 'substantially better performance per watt' vs. current state-of-the-art. The chip is the first in a multi-generation compute platform. Additionally, AVGO's TPU involvement at Google (displacing MediaTek in some configurations) was highlighted. Separately, JPM hosted an AVGO virtual NDR on July 7 with CEO Hock Tan. Multiple analysts view the Jalapeño announcement as validating the XPU diversification thesis and broadening Broadcom's addressable hyperscaler market.

bullets.title: DKNG: Launches DKeX exchange, PM volumes surging +265% YoY; JPM raises PT on World Cup traction
bullets.body: DraftKings completed its vertically integrated prediction markets stack with the launch of DKeX, a proprietary exchange. June consumer PM volumes tracked $200M+/week, up 80% from May's $110M, with $11.3B annualized total trading volume for the week of 6/21. ~30% of customers have used combos; DKeX provides ownership, speed-to-market, and improved operating economics. JPM maintained Overweight after the announcement, noting 300-400K PM customers acquired so far with bulk of NFL-season customers still ahead. NY OSB GGR tracking -17% YoY QTD but holds normalizing post-World Cup.

bullets.title: CCL: 2Q beat on costs but guides FY26 yields down 100bps; Middle East headwinds 'transitory'
bullets.body: Carnival reported 2Q adj. EPS of $0.41 vs. guidance of $0.34, beating on net cruise costs (+0.1% vs. guidance +2.6%). However, FY26 net yield guidance was reduced 100bps to +1.75% c/c due to prolonged Middle East conflict impact on European sailings. Management called June booking trends a 'turning point' and highlighted 2027 European bookings running mid-teens ahead of prior year. 93% booked for 2026 at historically high prices. UBS, JPM, and Citi all maintained Buy/OW ratings with $35-43 PTs. Stock fell ~4-5% on the guidance cut.

bullets.title: ACN: TD Cowen downgrades to Hold; AI disruption fears intensify as bookings decline
bullets.body: Accenture cut FY26 CC revenue growth guidance to +3-4% from +3-5% and reported managed services bookings down 3% CC y/y (second consecutive deceleration). TD Cowen downgraded to Hold, cutting PT to $150 from $258. Mizuho cut PT to $226 from $280. Multiple analysts flagged the read-through to IT Services peers (INFY down ~10%). UBS maintained Buy at $275 PT, viewing the $2B buyback boost to $7.5B total (~10% of market cap, 62% YoY increase) as a confidence signal. Stock traded at 8.5x 2Y forward P/E, a 20-year low per UBS.

bullets.title: NET/DDOG/CRM: Citi systems software scorecard bullish; upgrades NET/RBRK as strong executors
bullets.body: Citi's North America systems software post-C1Q26 report card showed stable-to-improving top-line trends. Most bullish on platform providers (DDOG, PANW, CRWD, DOCN) offering critical AI/agentic deployment scaffolding. DOCN showed the largest revenue CAGR increase (~13pts); DDOG showed the 2nd largest (~4pts) with NRR improving QoQ. NET and RBRK highlighted as strong executors with mission-critical use cases. Separately, Citi upgraded BOX/NAVN/APPN as new top picks in back-office software. INTU was effectively downgraded on AI displacement risk.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Joins DJIA replacing VZ; loses key AI researchers to Anthropic/OpenAI
bullets.body: Alphabet joins the DJIA effective June 29, replacing Verizon. However, the stock fell ~5-8% over the week as senior AI researchers John Jumper (Nobel laureate, AlphaFold co-creator) and Noam Shazeer departed for Anthropic and OpenAI respectively. Gemini 3.5 Pro was also delayed from June to July. PriceRunner antitrust judgment was postponed. MS streaming survey showed GOOGL YouTube with strongest engagement gains. GOOGL's DMA cloud gatekeeper designation by EU was also announced. Stock traded at 25x '26E EPS, -3% vs TTM average.

bullets.title: T/VZ: VZ wins AWS-3 spectrum reauction for $3.2B; AT&T raises administrative fee $1/line
bullets.body: Verizon won 82 licenses in major markets for $3.2B in the AWS-3 reauction, the largest winner in the $3.56B total auction. T-Mobile won 102 licenses. SpaceX planning Starlink mobile service for US consumers, flagged as potential competitive threat though T/VZ stocks were largely unchanged on the news. AT&T separately raised its Administrative & Regulatory Cost Recovery fee by $1/month to $4.99/line, generating ~$900M in annualized incremental revenue on ~75M postpaid lines—not in consensus estimates per KeyBanc Overweight.

bullets.title: AMD/ARM: UBS raises AMD PT to $670, ARM to $470 on agentic AI CPU demand shift
bullets.body: UBS raised AMD server CPU revenue estimate to $50B by C2030E (from $41B) as agentic AI drives architectural split: ARM favored for latency-sensitive head nodes (~70% share of 20M unit TAM), AMD for throughput-driven standalone racks. AMD assumed to capture 60% of standalone CPU segment vs. 40% ARM. AMD's Venice CPU could reach 6.75M units in 2027; NVDA's Vera CPU projected at 5.75M. ARM Gen1 AGI CPU limited by core count for standalone use; Gen2/Gen3 roadmap (200-500 cores) could expand. UBS separately noted QCOM upgraded to EW at MS and DZ Bank (PT $265) on data center pivot.

bullets.title: DLR/EQIX: DLR acquires $1.6B in Kansas City data center assets, Teraco stake; Citi maintains Buy
bullets.body: Digital Realty announced ~$1.6B in transactions: (1) ~$475M for 1,440 acres near Kansas City with 600MW initial capacity scaling to 2GW; (2) ~$650M to increase Teraco ownership to 77%; (3) ~$485M acquisition of Columbia Capital infrastructure platform with ~$9B AUM. Transactions funded via 6.3M share issuance at $197.54 avg. Citi maintains Buy on both DLR (PT $226) and EQIX (PT $1,240), noting Virginia's new $0.011/kWh electricity tax on data centers is manageable (~$14M max annual impact for EQIX) and largely passable to customers.

bullets.title: Goldman initiates US Towers: Buy AMT (PT $215), Neutral CCI/SBAC; sector reaccelerating to 3%+ growth
bullets.body: Goldman analyst Mike Ng initiated US tower sector coverage with Buy on AMT and Neutral on CCI/SBAC. US tower sector expected to inflect to 3%+ revenue growth from prior ~2% decline CAGR (2023-26E) driven by 3% annual escalators, new spectrum deployment, and densification. AMT positioned as organic growth leader with diversified global portfolio and growing CoreSite data center platform. CCI faces ~$220M DISH/EchoStar churn; SBAC faces near-term churn and refinancing pressures.

bullets.title: NFLX: Wolfe initiates Outperform at $107 PT; 19x '27 P/E attractive vs quality-growth blend
bullets.body: Wolfe Research initiated NFLX at Outperform with $107 PT, noting 19x '27 P/E is at-or-below historical averages for a company with ~15% revenue CAGR (2024-26E). MS's 16th annual streaming survey showed NFLX with strongest net retention score (+18), best original programming perception (31%), and rising ad-tier adoption (26% of respondents). Stock was down ~22.6% YTD creating the entry opportunity. Risk is META's Instagram TV expansion into long-form content. MS is OW DIS, NFLX, PSKY; EW WBD.

bullets.title: FIG: Citi upgrades to Buy at $36 PT on Config 2026; Config reinforces AI moat but margin concerns linger
bullets.body: Citi upgraded Figma to Buy with $36 PT (93% upside from $18.64) after Config 2026 unveiled AI agent-assisted tools (Code Layers, Motion, Shaders) designed to deepen engagement and drive seat mix toward premium. JPM maintained Neutral, flagging near-term gross margin pressure as new features are in free beta. Wolfe maintained Peer Perform at $15-$25 fair value range. The consensus is constructive on product roadmap but gross margin durability remains the key debate.

bullets.title: SHOP: ACN/UBS bullish on Campaigns monetization; SHOP +4.3% in Canada on week
bullets.body: UBS highlighted Shopify's Shop Campaigns as a potential long-term revenue driver, with merchants acquiring customers at attributable CAC via the Shop app. SHOP AI-referred shoppers convert 50% higher with 14% higher AOVs vs organic search; AI platform orders growing 13x y/y. SHOP was among the notable Canadian market gainers (+4.3% to C$165.15 on June 26). JPM separately positioned AMZN, GOOGL, and SHOP as the three primary beneficiaries of agentic commerce via the Universal Commerce Protocol.

bullets.title: AFRM: Morgan Stanley downgrades to Equal-Weight; Mizuho survey shows Walmart shoppers prefer Affirm 2x over Klarna
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley downgraded AFRM to Equal-Weight from Overweight, noting the market now properly reflects durability of growth, funding, and credit. However, Mizuho raised PT to $100 (from prior) after a proprietary survey of ~450 Walmart shoppers showed Affirm preferred 2:1 over Klarna for online BNPL, despite Klarna's 1+ year exclusivity at Walmart. AFRM CEO publicly alluded to volume at 'a very large retailer' continuing post-delisting. Stock was +8.1% mid-week before the Morgan Stanley downgrade.

bullets.title: MSFT: Technical breakdown below 200-DMA; Italian antitrust probe on 365 pricing; Xbox price hike #3
bullets.body: 22V and other technical analysts flagged MSFT with a Technical Score of 0/4, below the 200-DMA since February, and at 6.5-year relative lows vs. S&P 500 with risk to $250 if $350 support breaks. MSFT was also targeted by Italy's competition authority for allegedly forcing consumers onto a higher-priced Microsoft 365/Copilot tier without clear disclosure. Xbox prices were raised for the third time in 13 months ($100-$150 starting Aug 1) on memory/storage costs up 2.5x. MSFT is shifting AI strategy toward model choice and lower-cost inference.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Sky unit nearing £1.6B deal for ITV's Media & Entertainment business
bullets.body: Comcast's Sky unit is reportedly close to agreeing terms to acquire ITV's Media & Entertainment business for ~£1.6B (~$2.1B USD), with ITV Studios also acquiring Love Productions. The deal would create a larger UK streaming competitor. Separately, UBS's 2Q broadband preview for CMCSA models accelerating ARPU declines (-4.0% vs -3.1% in 1Q), 153K broadband losses, and modest wireless strength (+400K adds). UBS maintains Neutral rating. Broadband competition from fiber/FWA/satellite expected to persist.
